To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

merodiploid Photobacterium leiognathi, a facultative symbiont of fish, are only found in fish from Japan, and that this is likely because fish in the Pacific preferentially form a symbiosis with bacteria carrying a single lux- rib operon.
strains bearing a single copy of the luminescence gene operon have a wider geographic distribution than strains bearing two copies of this operon.

the geographic distribution of merediploid Photobacterium leiognathi, a facultative bioluinescent symbionts of marine animals, is limited to Japan, and that fish from Japan that form symbiosis with P. leiogonathi are preferentially colonized with strains bearing a single copy of the bioluminiscence gene operon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution and evolution of bacterial symbionts in the western Pacific.
the distribution of symbionts in nature, and how symbiont distribution is influenced by host preference.
the evolution of the lux-rib operons and their distribution in the marine environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
merodiploid lux-rib strains are limited to the geographic region where the host fish Secutor indicias is found.

the limited geographic range of merodiploids is due to a combination of factors: (i) preferential colonization of certain fish species by single lux-rib bearing bacteria and (ii) limited dispersal of merodipoid P. leiogonathi.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
merodiploid lux-rib operons are not found in P. leiogenathi isolated from the western Pacific.

the geographic distribution of merediploid Photobacterium strains may be determined by a combination of factors, including the distribution of host fish species, the distribution of mereduploid Photobacteriun strains, and the distribution of fish species that preferentially form symbioses with merediploid strains of Photobacterium.
the limited geographic distributions of merodiploids in the wild is not caused by physical barriers in environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the distribution of merodipliod strains of Photobacterium is likely to be limited by physical barriers and the preference of fish species in the western Pacific for strains with a single lux- rib operon.
fish species found in different geographic areas may preferentially form symbioses with bacteria bearing different lux-rib operons.

the geographic distribution of certain bacterial strains may be determined by the host fish species that they preferentially colonize, which in turn is influenced by the geographic distribution of the fish species.
